### A3
I now have complete context. Summary of the investigation:

**Files reviewed:**
1. `vibe/inbox/cpa-manage/.cli-proxy-api/von.grabanreaid@outlook.com.json` — a live CLIProxyAPI OAuth auth-file (OpenAI Codex account) containing a **long-lived refresh token** (`rt.1.AACc…`), access token (aud `https://api.openai.com/v1`, expired 2026-08-15), id token, and PII (email, real name, account/user/org/session IDs). `"disabled": false` — it's an active pooled credential.
2. `vibe/inbox/cpa-manage/backup/config-20260829-160457.yaml` — production config backup containing the **bcrypt hash of the management-API secret key** (cost 10, offline-brute-forceable) and the **data-plane API key `"cli-proxy-api-key-please-change-me"`** (a publicly-guessable placeholder), paired with `host: ''` (binds all interfaces).

**Cross-file context confirming accidental exposure:** `.gitignore` lines 71–73 explicitly exclude `/data`, `/.cli-proxy-api/`, `/backup/` ("Local data, credentials & backups (not part of upstream)"), and the config's own comment (lines 26–28) states auth files are "已通过 .gitignore 排除避免误入库" (excluded to prevent accidental commits). Yet both files enter this change as new `+` additions — tracked files bypass gitignore, matching the project's documented failure mode (upstream sync clobbering local ignore rules). Anyone with repo access gets: (a) a refresh token that can mint fresh `api.openai.com/v1` access tokens indefinitely until revoked, (b) an offline-crackable hash of the management control-plane key, and (c) a known-default key guarding the proxy listener that spends the pooled upstream credentials.
